clue.text: House where thousands help for nothing in Japan

definitions.note: the definition names a place located in Japan rather than a synonym for the country

parts.note: K stands for a thousand, so two of them give thousands
to help is to aid
O, the round figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A Japanese household where thousands pitch in unpaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word. The definition 'in Japan' is loose: it points to a place found in Japan.
explanation.definitionFit: Hokkaido is the large northern island of the Japanese archipelago, so it is a place located in that country.

clue.text: Novel conclusion of 19 10

definitions.meaning: a book by E. M. Forster, published in 1910
19 10 is PARTY LEADER; the downfall of Michael Howard, Conservative leader 2003-05, read as a possessive phrase

explanation.walkthrough: 19 and 10 cross-refer to PARTY and LEADER. Michael Howard led the British Conservative Party until 2005, so his finish is a fair second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The Forster novel about the Schlegel sisters and a country house is the first meaning; the second is a politician's career ending.

clue.text: 19 10, losing heart, confines pupil to Scots earldom in Scots town

indicators.note: confines means the shortened surname wraps round the following pieces
losing its heart means the central letter of the surname is dropped

parts.note: 19 10 is PARTY LEADER; Neil Kinnock led the British Labour Party in the 1980s
L, the learner plate, stands for a pupil
Mar is an ancient Scottish earldom

explanation.surface: A Labour politician shut a schoolchild inside a Scottish noble title in a Scottish town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' drops the central letter of the surname, and 'confines' wraps what is left round the pupil and earldom; 'to' simply joins those two. Mar is an old Scottish earldom, Kilmarnock an Ayrshire town.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilmarnock is a town in Ayrshire in south-west Scotland, home of a well-known football club.

clue.text: Everyone expressed satisfaction with God

parts.note: everyone is all
ah is a sound of contentment

explanation.surface: The whole congregation sighed happily at the deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Allah is the Arabic name for God used in Islam.

clue.text: An odd tea chef makes for a macabre affair

indicators.note: makes signals that the letters of the preceding words are worked into something new

explanation.surface: A strange cook turns out something gruesome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; 'odd' looks like the anagram signal but its letters are part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The dance of death is the medieval allegory of Death leading people of all ranks to the grave, a morbid spectacle.

clue.text: Protest by spouse of brave king

parts.note: in old Westerns a squaw was the wife of a Native American warrior or brave
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A complaint lodged by the wife of a warrior king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is a link word; 'brave' is a noun here, a warrior, not an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: To squawk is to complain loudly, a squealing protest.

clue.text: Mother of nest — no black Catholic on throne then?

definitions.meaning: the egg-laying female who founds a colony of stinging insects

definitions.text: no black Catholic on throne then?
definitions.meaning: read as a sentence, the monarch was a WASP, a White Anglo-Saxon Protestant: neither black nor Catholic

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into a sentence about a past monarch's identity.
explanation.definitionFit: The fertile female of a colony of stinging insects starts and rules the nest, its mother.

clue.text: Problem for a 19 10 initially

parts.note: 19 10 is PARTY LEADER; Iain Duncan Smith, Conservative leader 2001-03, is known by his initials IDS

explanation.surface: A difficulty that faces a political chief at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' does not take first letters of clue words; it asks for the leader known by his initials. 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The disease is a grave health problem, so the acronym serves as an example of one.

clue.text: Enterprise 10 at church

definitions.meaning: 10 is LEADER; Captain ... commands the starship Enterprise in Star Trek

explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word between the two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Captain James T. Kirk heads the starship crew, and in Scotland the parish church is called the kirk.

clue.text: Cub on return to base has brief spell of fun

indicators.note: on return asks for the word that follows to be read in the opposite direction

parts.note: base in the sense of mean or lowly is low
a fling is a short period of enjoyment

explanation.surface: A young scout back at headquarters enjoys a little fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on return to' turns LOW into WOL; 'has' is a link word. 'base' looks like a camp, but it means low.
explanation.definitionFit: A wolfling is a young wolf, exactly what a cub is.

clue.text: Article on songs heard

indicators.note: heard signals that the word is spoken rather than written

parts.note: Lieder are German art songs, as by Schubert

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about songs one has listened to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word. The definition is the newspaper sense: an editorial or leading article.
explanation.definitionFit: In British newspapers a leading article, the editorial, is called by this name.

clue.text: Making physical education photo soft porn's first bestseller

indicators.note: making signals that the letters of the following pieces are put together into a new form

parts.note: PE is the school abbreviation for physical education

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word porn's

explanation.surface: A gym photo turned into soft porn sells best.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram pool is PE, PHOTO, SOFT and P. Top of the Pops was the long-running BBC chart show, and a record at the top is the bestseller.
explanation.definitionFit: Being number one on the singles chart means a record is the bestseller of the week.

clue.text: Section of river by a lost field, new or second-hand?

parts.note: a reach is a stretch of a river between bends or locks

indicators.note: lost signals the single letter being removed from the field

parts.note: a meadow is a field

explanation.surface: A stretch of river next to a field: is it new or used?
explanation.walkthrough: 'lost' removes A from MEADOW to give MEDOW; 'by' and 'or' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A reach-me-down is a hand-me-down garment, bought ready-made or passed on, hence second-hand.

clue.text: "What The Papers Say" features boy swallowing container with drinks

indicators.note: swallowing means the name takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: Joe is a boy's name
an urn is a container
ales are drinks

explanation.surface: A TV review of the press shows a lad gulping down a vessel and some beers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins URN and ALES. What the Papers Say was a long-running British TV programme reviewing the press.
explanation.definitionFit: Journalese is the distinctive cliché-ridden style of newspaper writing, the hallmark of what the papers say.

clue.text: Support six feet with no head — ecstasy for the unadventurous

parts.note: a stay is a support, as in a ship's rigging

indicators.note: with no head signals the removal of the opening letter

parts.note: a fathom is a depth measure of six feet
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A support six feet high, beheaded, with a drug for the timid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with no head' removes F from FATHOM to give ATHOM; 'for the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone stay-at-home prefers not to travel or venture out, so is unadventurous.

clue.text: Correct relationship to go down noisily

indicators.note: noisily signals that the word is spoken aloud

parts.note: to sink is to go down

explanation.surface: A good relationship makes a loud collapse.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in synch means being properly aligned or coordinated, a correct relationship between things.

clue.text: Witch hazel is to follow meat with (say) lunch (say)

indicators.note: to follow puts the word is after the rest

parts.note: ham is a meat

indicators.note: the second say signals that a meal is only spoken, giving its sound

parts.note: lunch, for example, is a meal, and with joins it to the meat

explanation.surface: Witch hazel is meant to come after a ham lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins HAM to the sounded meal; the first '(say)' marks lunch as an example of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamamelis is the botanical genus name of witch hazel shrubs.

clue.text: Waste time playing with 19 10 keeping his 19 cut

indicators.note: keeping means the surname holds the next piece inside

parts.note: 19 10 is PARTY LEADER; Michael Foot led the British Labour Party 1980-83

indicators.note: cut signals the final letter is removed

parts.note: his party, 19 being PARTY, is Labour

explanation.surface: Fooling around with a politician who holds his trimmed-down party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' docks the last letter of the party name, and 'keeping' puts the remainder inside the leader's surname. 'his 19' is Michael Foot's own party, Labour; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To fool about is to mess around idly, wasting time in play.

clue.text: Refusal to answer number — how French!

parts.note: comment is the French for how

explanation.surface: Declining to reply to a figure with an exclamation in French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'how' looks like an exclamation, but it is translated into French.
explanation.definitionFit: The stock phrase used by officials asked difficult questions is a refusal to answer.

clue.text: Person privy to celebration

definitions.meaning: someone who is a participant in, or knows of, an agreement or plan

explanation.definitionFit: A party to a deal is someone involved in it, and a party is also a festive gathering.

clue.text: Skill at bringing up flagship, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a flagship is an example of a mother vessel leading other craft

explanation.definitionFit: Mothercraft is the skill of rearing children, and a mother craft is a ship that leads or supplies others, as a flagship may.

clue.text: 9 gets it at length

parts.note: 9 refers to WOLFLING, defined in its clue as a cub

explanation.surface: A young animal gets it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' and 'at' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A cubit is an ancient unit of length, the span from elbow to fingertip.

clue.text: See 23
Report of 19 10 getting peerage for World War I general

parts.note: an earl holds one of the ranks of the peerage

indicators.note: report signals that the surname is heard, not spelt

parts.note: 19 10 is PARTY LEADER; William Hague led the Conservative Party 1997-2001

explanation.surface: News that a party chief has been ennobled, for a wartime commander.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Douglas Haig, made an earl after the war, commanded the British forces on the Western Front.

clue.text: Ploughed fields can, without a bit of earth

definitions.note: the noun phrase stands for land fit for cultivation; the answer is used as a noun

indicators.note: bit of here takes the central letter of the five-letter word earth

parts.note: to be able is to can

explanation.surface: Tilled land is possible, without a speck of soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the pieces from 'a bit of earth' stand in front of the verb. The definition is the noun sense, arable land.
explanation.definitionFit: Arable land is cultivated for crops, so ploughed fields are what the word describes.

clue.text: Spades at card game or reversed hat

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for spades in card games
ombre is an old three-handed card game

indicators.note: reversed means the word or is read backwards

explanation.surface: A card player's spades, then a hat flipped around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A sombrero is a wide-brimmed Mexican hat.

clue.text: Look into spare cover for footwear

indicators.note: into places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: gash is slang for spare or surplus
lo is an old word meaning look

explanation.surface: Peer into a spare cover for shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A galosh is a rubber overshoe worn to protect shoes from wet.

clue.text: The Guardian's after a rest in a way

indicators.note: after places the newspaper's phrase behind the others

parts.note: to sit is to rest
a newspaper speaks of itself with the editorial we, so The Guardian's means we're

explanation.surface: The newspaper is after a break, in some fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: The Guardian writes with the editorial we, so The Guardian's is a contraction of we are.
explanation.definitionFit: As it were is a hedging phrase meaning so to speak, in a manner of speaking.
